checks.legal: News coverage of the Clean Elections and Attorney General investigations and her lawsuit (Arizona Mirror, KJZZ), Sept 11–30, 2026. Court status: Maricopa County Superior Court dismissed her suit Sept 30; Court of Appeals declined the case; Arizona Supreme Court agreed Oct 8 to hear it (Arizona Mirror, Oct 8). A news search on Oct 14 found no ruling yet. CourtListener, Justia and the Maricopa docket were not opened directly. No criminal charge against her was found.

legal.t: The Clean Elections Commission (unanimously, Aug 27, 2026) directed its director to finish investigating whether her campaign actually collected its $5 qualifying contributions. About 74% of 5,000 donor names were shared with two other campaigns; six listed donors told the Arizona Mirror they never gave. The campaign deposited the $5 total in one lump sum on May 4, the day it applied. Collins also alleges two unreported subcontractors. The Attorney General is also investigating (Mirror, Sept 11). Her attorney, Tim La Sota, denies fraud but acknowledged she violated Clean Elections rules by signing forms for contributions she did not personally collect, saying she was confused. Possible outcome: an order to repay up to $2.8M, from personal funds if campaign cash is short.
legal.status: Investigations pending; no commission finding or repayment order and no criminal charge as of Oct 14, 2026. Her suit was dismissed Sept 30 as premature, and the Court of Appeals then declined to take the case. On Oct 8 the Arizona Supreme Court agreed to hear it (conference set for Oct 14; no ruling found). The candidates refused to comply with commission subpoenas; on Oct 6 the commission denied their motion to quash and extended its civil investigation past the Oct 29 deadline. Her attorney says the letters forced the campaigns to suspend.
